rationale: The production roadmap requires a Redis-backed global rate limiter with per-role limits before AEIS can be production-ready. This change makes rate-limit counters atomic through the cache facade, adds role-aware API tiers, exposes the effective tier in response headers, and fails fast when staging/production use memory or non-Redis cache backends. It is D3 because it changes cross-cutting API behavior and production startup policy.

steps: Revert Cache.incr and strict Redis fail-fast behavior if deployment bootstrap cannot provide Redis yet.
Run rate_limit, cache and startup_check test groups.
Keep SYLION_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED blocked in production even if this change is reverted.

fidelity_test.description: Verify role-tier rate limits, atomic counter increments, strict Redis production policy and existing cache integrations.
pre_conditions: No live Redis service is required for unit tests.
Redis production policy is validated by startup/cache fail-fast tests.
Rate limit route tests use isolated Starlette apps and in-memory cache.
fidelity_test.expected_outcome: Role headers expose owner/security/operator/auditor/viewer budgets, heavy endpoints stay capped, Cache.incr is repeatable, and strict environments reject memory/non-Redis cache configuration.
